newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT - Brazil power sector estimates upped.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Brazil power sector estimates upped.

text.p: -- Paribas Corp said in a report it increased its net income forecasts for Brazil's power sector by 17 percent for 1997 and five percent for 1998.
-- "Our revised forecasts result from updates to our models based on the 1996 results as well as the recent tariff increases and new economic forecasts," said analyst Lawson Steele.
-- Steele said it maintained its buy recommendations for Cesp, Eletrobras, Eletropaulo, Light and its sell rating for Cemig and CPFL.
-- Also, he said he maintained Copel with a "no action" rating while Cerj remained "undiscovered."
-- "Our valuations continue to suggest that the sector is undervalued despite its rise of 16 percent since we recommended an overweight position," said Steele.
-- He expected a rise of 22 percent in absolute terms and five percent in relative terms by year's end.
-- Steele raised his 1997 earnings estimate for Cerj to $37 million from $5 million and cut his 1998 forecast to $80 million from $86 million.
-- He raised his 1998 earnings per share (EPS) estimate for Light by 11 percent to $33.48.
-- Eletrobras 1997 and 1998 EPS estimates were both raised 18 percent to $44.67 and $46.13 respectively, he said.
-- Steele revised his 1997 estimate for Cesp to show a $38.8 million profit versus a prior forecast of a $192 million loss.
-- He trimmed his 1997 EPS forecast for Eletropaulo by three percent to $9.98 and Copel by 15 percent to $0.75. He cut his 1998 EPS forecast for Copel by 17 percent to $0.77.
-- Steele reduced his EPS estimate for CPFL this year by 11 percent to $7.04 and by 22 percent to $10.12 in 1998.
-- LightPar 1997 EPS forecast was also cut by 23 percent to $22.09, he said.
-- Steele cut his 1997 EPS estimate for Cemig by five percent to $2.14 and by nine percent to $2.64 for 1998.
